_source_notes.lineup.reentryPolicy: STARTER_ONCE is a label, not a numeric value -- spec Sec.8 'Primary distinction: NFHS baseball re-entry is starter-centric. A starting player may be withdrawn and re-enter once in the same batting position. A substitute who is withdrawn does not receive an independent re-entry right.' The state machine that enforces this (per-player/slot reentryCount, SOFT_WARNING on a substitute's re-entry attempt) is P1+ engine work, not this ruleset document -- this field is the policy key the lineup service will branch on.
_source_notes.lineup.dhPolicy: Enumerates the three NFHS baseball modes (spec Sec.8.2: No DH / Traditional DH / Player-DH) as a single policy identifier; the per-mode behavior (fixed batting-slot relationship, linked defensive+DH status for Player/DH) is P1+ lineup-service logic, not ruleset data.
_source_notes.lineup.courtesyRunnerPolicy.enabled: SUPERSEDED (P2 followup, 2026-09-14, owner decision): the engine no longer gates courtesy-runner entry by this value at all -- lineup_service.enter_courtesy_runner() is a universal operator option for every association, any player, any time, replacing the jurisdiction-specific adoption model this field originally described. Left in place, still false, purely as a historical/documentary artifact; nothing reads it. The original spec framing (Sec.10 'Policy is jurisdiction-specific'; MHSAA's postseason-only, pitcher/catcher-only enablement per spec Sec.17.1) is what this decision explicitly replaces.
_source_notes.runnerControl.lookBackRule: false: baseball has no look-back rule (spec Sec.16 differences matrix: 'No softball look-back rule' under the baseball column -- read the other way, this documents that baseball itself has none. This is a genuine NFHS structural difference, not an unverified placeholder.
